_comment: FIELD PRESENCE, measured against the live vuelta-2026 pool on 2026-09-13, after the
race finished and all 21 stages were closed. This is SHAPE ONLY: field names and how
many documents carry each. No prose, no picks, no addresses.
WHAT IT IS FOR. tools-undefined-sweep.js uses it to tell a field that is ALWAYS
present from one that is SOMETIMES ABSENT. An unguarded read of an always-present
field is noise; an unguarded read of a sometimes-absent one is the defect that put
'The read undefined' on five stage cards and 'undefined' down 15 rows of the Note
column. The difference is not visible in the source, only in the data, which is why
a grep could never have found either.
REGENERATE from a signed-in owner board tab whenever the document shape changes,
and certainly when a new race starts. A stale fixture makes the gate weaker, not
wrong: it can only miss a newly-optional field, never invent one.

stage._source: pools/vuelta-2026/stages/*, AS THE BOARD SEES IT after buildCDF
_normalized: THE FIXTURE DESCRIBES CDF.stages, NOT THE RAW FIRESTORE DOCUMENT, and the
difference matters. buildCDF does Object.assign({n:Number(d.id)}, v), so `n` is
supplied from the document id whenever the document itself lacks it. Raw stage
docs 1, 2 and 3 genuinely have no `n` field, and an audit reading Firestore
directly sees three undefineds collapse into one null key. The BOARD never sees
that: every entry in STAGES has an `n`.
So `n` is listed under always, on purpose. Measuring the raw documents instead
produced eleven false failures against render sites that cannot fire.
A fixture for a gate must describe the data AT THE READ SITE, not at its source.
